name: TURBO Plus
author: Manuel Andre

provenance.note: credits_doc.asc identifies it as 'AMOS 1.3 TURBO extension library V1.9 — LAST PD RELEASE' by Manuel Andre, Berchem, Belgium.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified. The AMOS PD Library on CD (Weird Science, 1994), archive.org item cdrom-amospdcd. The disc's own Documents/Copyrights states Weird Science claims no copyright over the material, that parts are shareware with fees due, and that users should make no assumption that anything on it is public domain. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

notes: A later TURBO than turbo-plus-1.0 and earlier than 2.15. Its English doc set covers only 18 of its 87 keywords, so the documentation describes a subset rather than the library and the binary is what the other 69 have to be read from. TURBO Plus 2.15 is the release with a manual worth the name, covering 128 of 152. Explains all 57 ids observed in slot 12 across 60 programs of the AMOS PD CD corpus, so the id base is calibrated; slot 8's 16 ids are all but two explained by this table too, suggesting yet another build in circulation. Andrew Burton's AMOS Extensions List (kept at ultimateamiga.com, updated 2007-07-29), compiled from the AMOS-LIST archives 1994-1998, Amiga magazine clippings and coverdisk CDs. lists this separately from Turbo Plus, crediting it to Manuel Andre — which its own credits_doc.asc already confirmed. THE AMOS 1.3 BUILD IS ALSO HELD since 2026-08-12: TURBO1_9.LIB, 19,236 bytes, sha256 12f37f097a3bf026f3f9f30bd8dc7b91605bdb35ffabbe5ff4d206796b0081c4, out of aturbo.lha on kyzer.me.uk's AMOS Factory mirror (sources/kyzer-amosfactory/). Its token table is IDENTICAL to this one's, 89 entries, so the 260 bytes between the two builds are all code -- the same controlled comparison of what the two hosts need that int-1.0 offers. That archive's Pro build is byte-identical to APD600's, so it is the same release and not a variant. It also carries 28 demo programs the APD600 copy does not.
